{
  "screen_decision": "include",
  "screen_rationale": "The study performs a meta-analysis of 33 Parkinson's disease microarray studies to quantify the concordance of gene expression signatures between human studies and various animal models, reporting average concordance values and analyzing factors influencing agreement. This directly measures the agreement between animal model results and human clinical outcomes at a molecular level.",
  "arm": "methods-and-bias",
  "arm_evidence": "This study aims to determine the major factors of study design influencing the observed lack of concordance between microarray studies of PD, including species, tissue, platform, and sample size.",
  "therapeutic_areas": [
    "neurodegeneration"
  ],
  "areas_evidence": "The study focuses on Parkinson's disease (PD), a neurodegenerative disorder, and compares gene expression patterns in human patients and animal models of PD.",
  "model_type": "across-multiple-models",
  "model_evidence": "The study analyzes 33 Parkinson's disease microarray studies, including human studies, mouse models, and rat models, to assess concordance.",
  "species": [
    "mouse",
    "rat"
  ],
  "species_evidence": "The study explicitly compares gene expression signatures between human studies and 'mouse models' and 'rat models' of Parkinson's disease.",
  "endpoint_class": "secondary-biomarker",
  "endpoint_evidence": "The study quantifies concordance based on gene expression signatures, which are molecular biomarkers, and analyzes differential gene expression and biological pathway enrichment."
